claims.text: Amanatto and other sweets are made without artificial coloring or preservatives, following traditional handcrafted methods.

name: あまつぼ じもの亭 (Amatsubo Jimonotei)

claims.text: Sashimi seafood bowls are served with standard Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat.
All featured dishes are seafood-based and oden shares a bonito-dashi simmering broth, so there is no separation from animal ingredients.
The cafe's own site states it offers low-calorie menus with minimal allergens and many gluten-free options, reflecting its fermented-adzuki health concept.

name: カフェ 安江町ジャルダン (Cafe Yasuecho Jardin)

claims.text: Sweets such as scones and the kuzu milk pudding are prepared fresh to order, so the owner is closely involved in each dish and could be asked about ingredients in person.
Signature menu is wheat-heavy (napolitan pasta, pizza toast, ham pilaf, toast); shared kitchen with no documented allergen handling.
Dishes are built on ham, cheese, butter and dairy; no documented dairy-free or plant-based preparation.

name: キュリオ エスプレッソ ヴィンテージ デザイン (Curio Espresso and Vintage Design)

claims.text: Staff speak English, which makes it easier for a foreign visitor to ask about ingredients and allergens directly.
English-speaking owners and staff at an American-style cafe make communicating dietary needs straightforward.

name: 第六ギョーザの店 (Dairoku Gyoza no Mise)

claims.text: Gyoza wrappers are wheat-based and prepared in a shared kitchen; no gluten-free handling is documented.
Dishes and dipping rely on standard soy sauce (wheat-containing) and dashi typical of town-Chinese/izakaya cooking.
Menu is built around meat, seafood, and animal/fish dashi; no vegan preparation or separation is documented.

name: ファーメント カフェ (fArment Cafe)

claims.text: Menu is wheat-heavy (noodle-based vegan curries, tantanmen, cakes and tiramisu), so a shared kitchen handling flour and noodles is expected. No gluten-free precautions are documented.

This is a mixed vegan / non-vegan kitchen. The signature cheesecake is topped with Parmesan and dairy lattes are served, so vegan dishes are prepared in a kitchen that also handles cheese and dairy; no separate vegan prep is documented.
Offers a genuine, well-liked vegan menu (spicy vegan keema curry, green curry noodles, taco rice, vegan tantanmen) described as satisfying despite containing no meat.
